report.notes: fetch_url.py now chooses the refused-fetch message by refusal_code. Only the address-class codes (ADDRESS_NOT_PUBLIC, ADDRESS_TRANSITION_REFUSED, HOST_LOCAL_NAME, HOST_NUMERIC_AMBIGUOUS, HOST_SINGLE_LABEL) say 'private or local network'. DNS_FAILED and DNS_EMPTY say 'URI could not reach that URL.'. PORT_REFUSED, SCHEME_REFUSED, USERINFO_REFUSED and the invalid-URL codes each get accurate wording, and unknown codes get a neutral fallback. refusal_code is kept and no address appears in any message. USERINFO_REFUSED has its own message rather than the private one the reviewer suggested; moving it back is a one-line change. uri_web/safe_fetch.py is unchanged because its codes already distinguish the cases. The new test file had 5 failures and 5 passes against the f44f70a fetch_url.py (loaded from the scratchpad under the same module name, because stash and overwriting the file were not permitted). After the repair, tests/ssrf plus tests/web/test_w1_pipeline_citations_injection.py pass (85 passed). The production-tool case with a long-label host was not tested because it would need real DNS.
